“The Master said: Only when the year turns cold do we know…” — Confucius (Analects 9.28)

Verified English quotation. Primary source: Analects 9.28. Theme: character.

About Confucius

Confucius (Kong Qiu, 551–479 BCE) taught in the late Spring and Autumn period amid the Zhou order’s political fragmentation. Born in the state of Lu, he briefly held local office and then spent years seeking rulers who would adopt ritual-based, virtue-centered government.

How to read this passage

Across 4 recurring voices here (notably Arthur Schopenhauer and Heraclitus), character is framed through Confucianism and Voluntarism. Some passages define character; others warn how it fails; still others relocate it inside habit, community, or language. This passage enters that discussion through character.

Concepts in this quote

Character
Character appears in this archive as a live philosophical concern—not a slogan. These verified English passages show how thinkers treat character as a problem of judgment, practice, or explanation.
